title: next ignores dependency relations when filtering
description:
'pebbles next' returns issues that should be filtered out by their dependency relations.

Repro (run in any pebbles workspace):
- Create A and B as TODO bugs.
- pebbles link A required_for B
- pebbles next  # currently lists B (the dependent) instead of hiding it; and hides A (the predecessor) instead of listing it.

Symmetric problem for scheduled_before:
- pebbles link A scheduled_before B
- pebbles next  # currently lists B even though A is its incomplete predecessor.

Root cause:
- Operations::next in src/operations.rs:312-326 iterates issue.relationships looking for RequiredFor entries.
- Operations::add_relationship in src/operations.rs:212-218 stores relations only on the source side. So the predecessor's file has the RequiredFor entry; the dependent's file has nothing.
- Net effect for required_for: next checks the wrong end of the relation. It uses the dependent's status to decide whether to hide the predecessor, which is exactly inverted from what it should do.
- scheduled_before is not checked at all.

That show works correctly:
- pebbles show <id> already reports incoming relations correctly (e.g. 'requires', 'scheduled after') by using Operations::get_incoming_relationships in src/operations.rs:471-494, which scans all issues for relations pointing at the given issue.

Implementation proposal:
- Have next use the same incoming-relationship logic that show uses (extract a shared helper if needed). Concretely: for each TODO candidate, consult its incoming relations; treat an incoming required_for from a non-Done issue as a hard blocker; either treat scheduled_before similarly or document the chosen semantics (see open questions).
- Performance note: a naïve per-issue call to get_incoming_relationships re-scans all issues each time (O(n^2)). Since next already loads all issues once at src/operations.rs:304, prefer building a reverse-relationship map (target_id -> Vec<(source_id, source_status, relation_type)>) once from that single load, then looking each candidate up in the map. This keeps next O(n) and avoids regressions on large workspaces.

Expected behavior:
- An issue with at least one incoming required_for relation from a non-Done issue is hidden from next.
- An issue with at least one incoming scheduled_before relation from a non-Done issue is at least clearly handled (see below).

Open questions (to explore when fixing):
1. scheduled_before semantics: hard filter (mirror required_for) or soft hint (don't hide, but order accordingly)? Today the help text 'actionable TODO issues with no blockers' reads as a hard guarantee; pick a semantic and reflect it in --help and SPEC.md.
2. Whether to expose the shared helper as a public Operations method (e.g. reverse_index() -> HashMap<Uuid, Vec<...>>) or keep it private to operations.rs.
3. Whether next should also surface why something is unblocked vs blocked (e.g. an optional --explain flag), or keep the output minimal.
